request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people, claims and pools exports now use the as-of figures while an as-of date is set. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests, including "as of exports", the one that failed before.

**What was wrong:** the server already answers reads as of the date the screen sends. But setting an as-of date clears all the screen's loaded data before re-reading it. The people and claims exports built their file from that data right away, so pressing them straight after setting a date gave a file with only the header line.

**The fix (front end only):**
- `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`: when pressed, each export re-reads the data it needs first, using the as-of date that is set at that moment. Then it builds the file. The pools export already re-read its data; it now does it the same way as the other two.
- `src/main/frontend/features/rates/useDueTotals.ts`: I took the due-total calculation out of the hook into a plain function, so the people export can run it on the data it just re-read. The screen's due-totals use the same function and work as before.

No server, stored-data or audit changes were needed. Because each export now re-reads first, the download starts a moment after the button is pressed.
